title: sprite.ts: SymbolInstance clip actions and loopMode/firstFrame silently dropped in symbol timelines
description:
packages/swf/src/sprite.ts has no support for encoding clip actions (onClipEvent handlers) or graphic symbol loopMode/firstFrame on SymbolInstance objects inside MovieClip symbol timelines. This causes two related runtime failures:

BUG A — Clip actions dropped:
When a SymbolInstance inside a symbol timeline has clipActions (onClipEvent handlers), sprite.ts never calls encodePlaceObject2WithClipActions. The PlaceObject2 tag is emitted without HasClipActions, so Ruffle never runs any onClipEvent code for nested instances.

BUG B — Graphic symbol loopMode/firstFrame ignored:
compile.ts handles loopMode ('loop'/'play-once'/'single-frame') and firstFrame by synthesizing clip actions (enterFrame→stop() for play-once, load→gotoAndStop(N) for single-frame) — see compile.ts lines 2058-2098. sprite.ts has no loopMode/firstFrame handling, so graphic symbol instances nested inside MovieClip timelines always loop regardless of the authored setting.

Root cause: both features require clip-action encoding (encodePlaceObject2WithClipActions / encodePlaceObject2MoveWithClipActions) which is only implemented in compile.ts.

Fix: In sprite.ts, add clip-action encoding for SymbolInstance:
1. Import encodePlaceObject2WithClipActions and encodePlaceObject2MoveWithClipActions from shapes.js.
2. Port the loopMode/firstFrame → effectiveClipActions synthesis from compile.ts (lines 2058-2098) into a shared helper function. Call it from both compile.ts and sprite.ts.
3. In the sprite.ts placement pass (lines 295-420), when a SymbolInstance has non-empty effectiveClipActions, use encodePlaceObject2WithClipActions instead of encodePlaceObject2.
4. In the posChanged move pass, use encodePlaceObject2MoveWithClipActions when clip actions are present.

Note: ClipActions also require the SWF header flag HasClipActions on the enclosing SWF. This flag is set in the main compile.ts SWF header. Nested sprites can legally contain PlaceObject2 with HasClipActions — Ruffle handles them correctly.

Related: task 1123 covers the analogous gap for frame sounds (frame.sound → StartSound) in sprite timelines.
